name.common: Construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza
otherNames: Building of the Pyramid of Khufu
meaningOfNames: Possibly named due to the shape resembling a cake of roasted wheat-grains preserved in honey, and in this sense is said to derive from pyros 'wheat' on the model of sesamis.
longFormInfo: The construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza refers to the building of the largest of the three main pyramids located on the Giza Plateau near Cairo, Egypt.
The construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza is believed to have started around 2580 BCE during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom of Egypt.

location.description: On the Giza plateau, located on the west bank of the Nile River. This site was close to the ancient Egyptian capital of Memphis

longFormInfo: The construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza is estimated to have been completed around 2560 BCE.

location.description: Contruction finished at the same location.

keyActorsOrParticipants: Names of individual architects and workers are not well-documented
causes: The construction of the Great Pyramids was primarily motivated by religious, political, and cultural factors.

In ancient Egyptian society, the construction of monumental tombs, such as pyramids, was seen as a crucial aspect of ensuring the pharaoh's transition to the afterlife and maintaining his divine status.
Grandiose monuments served to reinforce the pharaoh's power and authority over his subjects, as well as to showcase the wealth and capabilities of the Egyptian state
consequences: In the short term, it provided employment and economic opportunities for the workforce involved in its construction, while also contributing to the development of engineering and architectural techniques
The immense resources and labour required for its construction likely placed a strain on the Egyptian economy and society.
historiography: Over time, scholars have developed various theories and interpretations regarding its construction techniques, purpose, and cultural significance.
Early interpretations often emphasised mystical or esoteric explanations, attributing the pyramid's construction to supernatural forces or lost civilisations
Recently, archaeological evidence and scholarly research have shed light on the practical aspects of pyramid construction.
significance: The Great Pyramid of Giza is one of the most iconic and enduring symbols of ancient Egyptian civilization, showcasing the architectural and engineering prowess of the ancient Egyptians.
legacy: The construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza has left a lasting legacy in the fields of architecture, engineering, and archaeology, inspiring awe and fascination for millennia.
shortSummary: The construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza took place during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom of Egypt.
longSummary: The Great Pyramid was built for Pharaoh Khufu. It is believed to have been constructed over a 20-year period and was originally 146.6 meters (481 feet) tall, making it the tallest man-made structure in the world for over 3,800 years.
The construction process involved thousands of labourers, skilled craftsmen, and precise engineering techniques to create these impressive structures that have stood the test of time.

The construction of the pyramids, including the Great Pyramid of Giza, likely involved quarrying, transporting, and stacking massive limestone blocks to form the core structure using a combination of sledges, ramps, and leverage systems, with the outer casing stones added for a smooth finish, showcasing the meticulous craftsmanship and engineering prowess of the ancient Egyptians.

participants.name: Khufu
participants.role: the pharaoh for whom it was built

participants.name: Hemiunu
participants.role: vizier, traditionally credited as its architect
